flow.text: A 3-4-5 triangle with every vertex named, every side measured, and the right angle marked. Vertex labels, side labels and the right-angle square must all clear the arms and each other.

blocks.title: Right triangle 3-4-5
blocks.caption: Vertex labels, computed side lengths, and a right-angle marker at $A$.

slides.title: Angle arcs — single, multiple, and every vertex

flow.text: A scalene triangle with one double arc, one single arc, and a measured angle at each remaining vertex. Stacked arcs at one vertex must not overlap, and each arc must sit inside its own angle.

blocks.title: Scalene triangle with angle arcs
blocks.caption: Angle measures are computed from the construction, never authored.

slides.title: Stacked arcs on a short arm — correctness stress

flow.text: A sliver triangle whose arms are far shorter than the base arc radius, carrying three stacked arcs at the tight vertex. The radius clamp must still resolve to three distinct arcs inside the angle — clamping each independently collapses them onto one radius, which a figure with generous arms never reveals.

blocks.title: Stress — three arcs on a ~6px arm
blocks.caption: CORRECTNESS STRESS, not a visual exemplar. The arm at B is about 6px on screen, so the arcs are far too small to read — the only assertion is that they stay attached to the arms and stay distinct. Legibility is proven by the realistic case on the next page.

blocks.title: Where a student has to read it

flow.text: The companion to the stress case. The arm at B is genuinely short — short enough that the radius clamp is active — but the figure is one a lesson could actually use, so three stacked arcs must be distinguishable to a human at normal rendered size, not merely distinct as floats.

blocks.title: Three arcs on a genuinely small angle
blocks.caption: VISUAL QUALITY case. The arm at B is about 44px, so the clamp is active and the stack still resolves to three arcs a reader can count.

flow.text: The same right angle, rotated off the axes. The marker is built from the two incident rays, so it must follow the rotation rather than staying square to the grid.

blocks.title: Right angle at an arbitrary orientation
blocks.caption: The marker is derived from the rays $VP$ and $VQ$, not painted axis-aligned.

flow.text: A quadrilateral and a seven-sided irregular polygon, both through the same polygon renderer — no per-shape branch.

blocks.title: Quadrilateral with interior angles
blocks.caption: Four vertices, every interior angle measured.

flow.text: A tight polygon carrying vertex names, every side measured and every angle measured at once — the geometry equivalent of the crowded plane. Then the same figure with long descriptive side names instead of numbers.

blocks.title: Crowded — names, sides and angles together
blocks.caption: Stress case for the Stage-2c nearest-legal placement on geometry anchors.

blocks.title: Long identifiers on a small triangle
blocks.caption: Wide pills clear far less easily than a single digit.

slides.title: Concave polygon — the reflex vertex is reported, not measured

flow.text: Contract 8 says the (n−2)·180° sum is asserted on CONVEX fixtures and the reflex-vertex ERROR on a concave one — but until now there was no concave fixture, so half of that contract was asserted against nothing. A dart has one reflex interior angle; `figGeomAngle` returns the unsigned smaller sweep and so cannot express it, and the engine must say so rather than print 360−θ as though it were the interior angle.

blocks.title: Dart — one reflex interior angle
blocks.caption: The reflex vertex is reported and left unmeasured; the other three are measured normally.

slides.title: Reversed winding — same figure, vertices listed the other way

blocks.title: Winding must not decide the outside

flow.text: The same quadrilateral twice: once with its vertices listed clockwise and once anticlockwise. Every side measure must sit outside the outline and every interior angle inside it in BOTH, because "outside" is a property of the shape rather than of the order an author happened to type.

blocks.title: Quadrilateral — one winding
blocks.caption: Vertices listed A, B, C, D.

blocks.title: Quadrilateral — reversed winding
blocks.caption: The identical shape, listed D, C, B, A.

flow.text: A polygon authored hard against a stated domain, so every vertex label's outward direction leaves the canvas. Auto-fit must expand rather than let a pill run off the plane.

blocks.title: Polygon at the domain edge
blocks.caption: Edge case — an on-canvas constraint at every vertex.

slides.title: Parameterised construction and an author error

flow.text: A triangle solved from three side lengths through the Stage-1c construction DAG, and an impossible one that must be reported rather than drawn.

blocks.title: triangleSSS 7-8-9
blocks.caption: Solved from givens, not authored coordinates.

blocks.title: Author error state
blocks.caption: Impossible construction givens, an unknown vertex, a right-angle assertion that is not 90°, and a zero-length arm.
